title: id(currency): RateAuthorisation::validate checks only issuer and rate_den — inverted amount bounds, empty/inverted validity window, >100% fee_bps, zero rate and same-ledger bodies all fold Live, and a malformed higher version shadows a good one

body:
## Problem

In `pkgs/id/src/currency.rs`, `RateAuthorisation::validate` is the only validity gate the fold trusts — and it checks exactly two things (issuer match, `rate_den != 0`). Every other validity condition the type's own field docs state is never checked anywhere, `sign_authorisation` never calls `validate` at all, and the fold crowns the highest "valid" version — so a malformed authorisation signs, folds `Live`, and a malformed higher version permanently shadows a good lower one (the fold doc: no older version revives once a higher exists).

- `pkgs/id/src/currency.rs:152-163` — `validate()` checks only `issuer_id == author` and `rate_den == 0`. Its rustdoc (:146-151) names only those two errors, matching the one field with explicit validity language: `rate_den` is "non-zero in a valid authorisation" (:104-106).
- The unchecked documented conditions: `min_amount` is the "Smallest convertible amount" and `max_amount` the "Largest" (:108-112) — `min > max` is a contradiction no conversion can satisfy; `not_before` is "No conversions before this time" and `expires_at` the "Mandatory expiry: no conversions at or after" (:118-121) — `expires_at <= not_before` is an empty/inverted window; `fee_bps` is a "fee in basis points" (:124-126) — above 10,000 bps the fee exceeds 100% of the conversion; the module doc (:10-14) defines the object as one direction `source_ledger` → `dest_ledger` — identical ledgers are a degenerate self-conversion; `rate_num == 0` makes `apply_rate` return `Some(0)` for every amount (:169-175).
- `pkgs/id/src/currency.rs:279-311` — `fold_authorisation` filters candidates by `body.validate(author).is_ok()` (:291, under the doc at :262-277: "Among the expected issuer's valid versions the highest is the candidate") and crowns the highest version `Live`. An unchecked-malformed v2 therefore displaces a good v1, and since revocation/supersession never revives a lower version, the authorisation is bricked by its own malformed successor.
- `pkgs/id/src/currency.rs:313-336` — `sign_authorisation` serializes and signs any body without calling `validate`: even the two existing checks are sign-time unenforced, so an issuer can publish a zero-denominator authorisation the fold will silently drop (`fold` → `None`) while believing it live.

This is Phase 1 library code (#3800, closed), but the Phase 2/3 gateway (#3801/#3802, on #2290) will consume `fold_authorisation`'s `Live` state as its trust input — the gate should mean what the docs say before a gateway builds on it.

## Evidence (verified this run)

Laptop probe `~/git/fleet/probe-2026-11-02-laneB-currencyvalidate/` with `currency.rs` copied verbatim from `pkgs/id/src/currency.rs` (production code, md5 `291c105842289c856635a2b69ffd1d72`, identical in the sandbox clone at main `a0ff47b41` and the laptop checkout; only the `#[cfg(test)]` module was stripped and `crate::chain` stubbed to the surface `currency.rs` uses — `validate`/`fold_authorisation`/`apply_rate` are pure and unmodified), `cargo run --release`, using the #2290 worked example from the module's own tests as the baseline body:

- BASELINE (min 1 ≤ max 10,000, window 0 → 4102444800, no fee): `validate=Ok(())`, fold = `Live`.
- P1 `min_amount=10_001, max_amount=10_000`: `validate=Ok(())`, fold = `Live`.
- P2 `not_before=1000, expires_at=1000` (empty window): `validate=Ok(())`, fold = `Live`.
- P3 `not_before=2000, expires_at=1000` (inverted window): `validate=Ok(())`, fold = `Live`.
- P4 `fee_bps=Some(20_000)` (a 200% fee): `validate=Ok(())`, fold = `Live`.
- P5 `rate_num=0`: `validate=Ok(())`, `apply_rate(100)=Some(0)`, fold = `Live`.
- P6 `source_ledger == dest_ledger == "ABC"`: `validate=Ok(())`, fold = `Live`.
- CONTROL `rate_den=0`: `validate=Err(ZeroRateDenominator)`, fold = `None` — the one documented check beyond issuer works.
- P7 shadowing: good v1 + inverted-bounds v2 → fold = `Live` version 2 (min 10001, max 10000); the good v1 is unreachable.

Dedup: title/keyword searches for `RateAuthorisation`, currency-validate, fee_bps and min_amount across open and closed issues find only the #2290 design (open), the closed Phase 1 implementation #3800, and the gateway phases #3801/#3802 — none covers validation completeness.

## Why it matters

`Live` is the fold's promise that an authorisation is usable. Today it also covers authorisations that can never convert (inverted bounds, empty window), that charge more than the converted amount in fees, or that convert a ledger into itself — and because version selection trusts `validate`, one malformed successor silently retires every good earlier version. The issuer-side sign path compounds it: nothing stops publishing a body the fold will drop or crown wrongly. Fixing the gate now is cheap; after the #3801/#3802 gateway treats `Live` as authoritative, each unchecked case becomes a gateway bug instead of a library inconsistency.

## Acceptance criteria

- `RateAuthorisation::validate` rejects, with named `ValidateError` variants: `min_amount > max_amount`; `expires_at <= not_before`; `fee_bps > 10_000`. For `rate_num == 0` and `source_ledger == dest_ledger`, the fix either rejects them in `validate` too or documents explicitly at the field why they are intentionally valid — silence is not an accepted outcome.
- `sign_authorisation` refuses a body that `validate` rejects (sign/validate symmetry), or the asymmetry is documented as intentional at `sign_authorisation` with the reason.
- New unit tests cover each rejected case at both `validate` and the fold (a malformed higher version no longer crowns over a good lower version — it is skipped by the fold's validity filter, like the zero-denominator control), and the existing `currency` tests pass unchanged.
- The `validate` rustdoc lists every condition it checks, so the Phase 2 gateway (#3801/#3802) can rely on the doc as the contract.
